note_claims.claim: The patient presented with central chest pain starting at about 11:00 while gardening.
The patient experienced heavy central chest pain radiating to the left arm, lasting about 30 minutes, and is currently experiencing pain at a severity of 3/10.
The patient has associated sweating and mild breathlessness, but no nausea.
The patient has no previous similar episodes or known cardiac disease.
The patient has hypertension.
The patient is a smoker, smoking about 20 cigarettes per day.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 52.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 60.
The patient received 300 mg of aspirin and a GTN spray from the ambulance crew.
The patient is taking amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The patient's blood pressure is 152/90.
The patient's oxygen level is 97 percent on air.
The patient's heart sounds are normal.
The patient's chest is clear.
There is no swelling in the patient's ankles.
The ECG shows ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6, measuring about one millimetre.
The clinical impression is suspected acute coronary syndrome (possible NSTEMI).
The plan includes serial high-sensitivity troponin testing.
The plan is to start fondaparinux 2.5 mg subcutaneously once daily to thin the blood.
The plan includes using a GTN spray if the pain returns.
The patient will be admitted under the cardiology team, with a likely plan for a coronary angiography.
The patient was instructed to report recurrent or worsening pain to nursing staff immediately.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reported getting pain in the chest while digging in the garden.
The pain started after lunch, but the patient corrected this to 'before' lunch, stating they hadn't eaten yet, around 11:00.
The patient described the pain as being in the middle of the chest, like a heavy weight.
The pain radiated down the patient's left arm.
The pain lasted about half an hour and is currently at a severity of three out of ten.
The patient felt very sweaty but not sick.
The patient reported feeling 'a bit' short of breath.
The patient stated they have never had anything like this before.
The patient has no heart problems in the past, only blood pressure.
The patient is on amlodipine 5 milligrams.
The patient confirmed they have no other medicines.
The patient confirmed they have no known drug allergies.
The patient smokes about twenty cigarettes a day.
The patient's father had a heart attack at age 52.
The relative stated their father had a heart attack at age 60.
The paramedics gave the patient aspirin 300 milligrams and a GTN spray.
Examination findings: Heart rate is 88 and regular, blood pressure is 152/90, heart sounds are normal, chest is clear, and oxygen level is 97 percent.
ECG findings: The heart tracing shows about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
The clinician suggested the possibility of acute coronary syndrome (possible NSTEMI) and that a blood test for troponin was taken.
The clinician planned to start an injection of fondaparinux 2.5 milligrams under the skin once a day to thin the blood.
The clinician advised the patient to have a GTN spray if the pain comes back.
The clinician planned to admit the patient under the cardiology team, who will likely want to perform an angiogram.
The clinician planned to repeat the ECG every time the patient gets pain.
The clinician instructed the patient to tell the nurses straight away if the pain comes back or gets worse.
